messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate on /v1/generate (us-west2) - 5xx spike, 18% errors in last 5m. Suspected: serving runtime crashes.
ops-oncall-Alex: saw it. killing errors show container restarts on a few nodes. digging into logs now.
ops-oncall-Alex: kubectl get pods -n redwood-serving | grep crash | wc -l -> 6
sre-Li: can you paste the pod logs for one of the failures?
ops-oncall-Alex: here's stdout from pod gpu-srv-13-ptx:
```
[2024-06-02T14:05:11Z] ERROR: runtime: CUDA illegal memory access at address 0x7f1a2c3bf000
[2024-06-02T14:05:11Z] stack: 0x7f1a2c3bef0 -> kernel.cu:line 423
[2024-06-02T14:05:11Z] aborting process due to illegal device pointer (misaligned address)
[2024-06-02T14:05:11Z] note: next message: OOM while handling large batch (seq_len=2048)
```
eng-runtime-Maya: that's the misaligned device pointer we saw in previous paging incidents. looks correlated with burst autoscaling + large batch sizes.
eng-ml-Raj: model variant is the 7B fp16 variant on that node. sequence length distribution spiked because a customer replayed long prompts.
support-Jenna: customer Eric from AcmeCorp reported increased latency then 500s ~14:04 UTC — they saw ~6% failed requests, mostly in us-west2. CS contacted them and they confirmed heavy batch scoring job started at 14:00.
customer-success-Eric: confirmed. they kicked off a backfill to index embeddings. asked if any ETA to recovery.
ops-oncall-Alex: immediate mitigation plan: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) route new traffic to fallback quantized variant (less memory), 3) restart failed pods after drain, 4) roll back large-batch routing for tenant.
sre-Li: taking over incident. will coordinate node cordon/drain. Alex, post node list.
ops-oncall-Alex: nodes: gpu-node-usw2-13, gpu-node-usw2-14, gpu-node-usw2-21. cordoning now.
infra-operator-Nash: ack — cordoned 3 nodes. starting drains. note: pod evictions will trigger migrations to other racks, might increase transient CPU.
eng-runtime-Maya: in parallel, pushing routing override to route A/B to quantized-v2 model for any request >1024 tokens. command: POST /control/routing -> {"policy":"prefers-quantized-v2","condition":"seq_len>1024"}
eng-ml-Raj: done. traffic shifted ~70% away from affected nodes.
ops-oncall-Alex: restarted 6 failed pods after drain. most came up but two still crash-looping. grabbing coredumps.
ops-oncall-Alex: gdb info from one coredump: 
```
#0  0x00007f1c2b1a in cudaMemcpyAsync_impl() from /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so
#1  0x0000560f1a2e in kv_cache::write_chunk (args...) at kv_cache.cc:312
#2  0x0000560f1a8f in model_infer::dispatch at infer.cc:742
#3  0x0000560f1b11 in worker_loop at worker.cc:198
```
sre-Li: pattern: writes to KV cache during high-concurrency pagewalks -> illegal device pointer -> kernel abort. Could be a kernel/driver race or a device pointer becoming invalid during an eviction.
eng-runtime-Maya: temporary runtime patch: add checks for device pointer alignment and guard early returns to avoid invalid memcpy. deploying hotfix to canary.
eng-runtime-Maya: hotfix deployed to canary (gpu-srv-canary-4). running synthetic long-seq workload now.
ops-oncall-Alex: canary passed for 15m, no illegal accesses. rolling hotfix to a subset of nodes (2/9 in us-west2) and keeping cordon on remaining original nodes.
sre-Li: customer impact update: roughly 120 unique requests failed during spike, mostly high-seq batch jobs. impacted tenants: AcmeCorp and 2 smaller customers. SLA impact minimal but visible. CS notified AcmeCorp at 14:22 UTC.
support-Jenna: I've opened a support ticket and offered compensatory credits. Acme replied they're fine with rollback & mitigation.
eng-ml-Raj: long-term actions: 1) add device-pointer lifetime checks in runtime, 2) instrument KV cache for concurrent eviction races, 3) run kernel-driver stress tests with high sequence concurrency, 4) consider limiting default max batch size for hosted until validated.
sre-Li: follow-up items for postmortem: collect dmesg and driver logs from affected nodes, enable cuda-memcheck on repro cluster, gather coredumps and uploads to GCS (path: gs://redwood-incident-1717345123/).
ops-oncall-Alex: uploaded 2 coredumps and logs to bucket. link: https://console.gcs/redwood-incident-1717345123 (internal)
eng-runtime-Maya: filing PR for runtime guard and unit tests. will include perf gates.
eng-ml-Raj: also adding a model-side limiter: reject requests >2048 tokens for hosted until we validate fallback path.
sre-Li: handing off to eng-runtime Maya and eng-ml Raj for root cause and fix verification. Oncall remains closed but will watch metrics for 2 hours.
ops-oncall-Alex: leaving detailed timeline in incident tracker. Marking incident priority P2 (partial customer impact).
customer-success-Eric: thanks everyone. I'll update Acme with the mitigation summary and next steps.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status -> Mitigated. Postmortem owner: eng-runtime-Maya. SLA impact: limited.
eng-runtime-Maya: assigning postmortem; will coordinate with SRE and ML. planned RFC for KV cache pointer model next week.
sre-Li: closing channel handoff. If we see recurrence, escalate to kernel/driver team.
ops-oncall-Alex: thanks team.
